items.inspect: Open frame 1 at full size beside the logged input image. Same character, same design, before judging any later frame. A wrong frame 1 means the reference never anchored (a distinct failure from drift) and the run is a FAIL regardless of later frames.
items.item: For generated work: frame 1 is the correct character, anchored to the reference that was actually fed — the run record logs the exact input image and its sha256.
items.name: frame-1-reference-anchored

items.inspect: Every pose at full size: in a profile walk exactly one eye is visible and the gaze runs along the direction of travel, never out at the viewer.
items.item: Front face on a profile body: both eyes, front nose and mouth, staring at the viewer while the body moves sideways.
items.name: front-face-on-profile-body

items.inspect: The torso must read as the SIDE of the garment: one strap line, fastenings edge-on, side silhouette. If the chest reads as a portrait, the item fails.
items.item: Front torso on profile legs: the torso keeps its front arrangement (both straps, waist items spread across the chest, chest details facing front) over legs that walk sideways.
items.name: front-torso-on-profile-legs

items.inspect: The head-to-collar join in every pose, at full size, on light and dark grounds. Any visible bite out of the neck or jaw line fails.
items.item: A notch or gap cut into the jaw/neck where the head crop meets the collar.
items.name: neck-notch-gap

items.inspect: Both tails (or the design's full hair mass) accounted for and placed for the side read; the silhouette from the side is a side silhouette, not the portrait's outline.
items.item: Hair keeps its front-view arrangement on a turned head — a tail hanging over the chest as in the portrait, the second tail lost or merged into whatever is behind it.
items.name: hair-front-arrangement

items.inspect: Hands present and shaped; the near arm swings against the near leg (arm forward when the same-side leg is back), measured or read off the poses — not asserted.
items.item: The near arm is a stiff diagonal slab across the torso: no hand, no swing, no opposition to the legs.
items.name: arm-slab

items.inspect: Both feet in every contact pose: toe along the direction of travel, sole planted on the ground line. One viewer-facing foot fails the item.
items.item: The planted shoe faces the viewer (a front shoe head-on) while the other shoe points along travel — two feet pointing two different directions.
items.name: shoe-direction-disagreement

items.inspect: Foot clearance at the high-point poses, in pixels, compared against the contacts. A lifted knee/foot at step-over height in an ordinary walk fails.
items.item: High points step march-high, like a parade step, instead of passing low the way a walk passes.
items.name: march-high-points

items.inspect: Near AND far arms both present in the construction and visible in the poses, the far arm offset (and shaded per the side convention), swinging in opposition to the near arm.
items.item: The far arm does not exist — the figure has only one arm.
items.name: far-arm-missing

items.inspect: Every clip/tie at full size: seated ON the hair mass, in a position that makes sense from the side, attached in every pose. One floater fails.
items.item: Hair furniture (clips, scrunchies, ties) floats on or off the hair as front-view stickers — including a bobble hanging detached in mid-air.
items.name: hair-furniture-floats

items.inspect: The profile head carries only what a profile shows. Anything that only makes sense from the front fails.
items.item: Far-side face furniture from the front portrait persists at the wrong edge of a profile head (far ear, earring, second-eye elements).
items.name: far-side-face-furniture

items.inspect: Items recede in profile: near item full, far items partial behind it. In EVERY pose, no item is hidden behind a limb and no contents face the viewer.
items.item: Carried items (the waist jars) hang in a front row at one depth, contents facing out — and in some poses one is buried behind the arm.
items.name: jars-at-one-depth

items.inspect: The skirt wraps to a side silhouette; the hem differs across poses (charted sway); no solve slash or cut line crosses it in any pose.
items.item: A front skirt on a side figure: symmetrical pleats, straight front hem, identical in every pose, with a hard slash where a leg solve crosses it.
items.name: skirt-front-static

items.inspect: Both passing poses: near/far is unambiguous — far leg treated (darker, marginally smaller/higher per the settei convention) and the overlap order reads correctly.
items.item: Legs in one identical flat colour: at crossings you cannot tell which leg is in front, and the far shoe at the same size reads in front of the near one.
items.name: legs-do-not-separate

items.inspect: Across the cycle: tails/hair carry charted secondary motion (lag/settle behind the stride, small per-pose offsets). Pixel-identical hair across poses fails.
items.item: Hair and tails are identical in every pose — a statue's hair on a walking body. No sway, no settle, no lag.
items.name: hair-frozen-no-secondary-motion

items.inspect: A blink occurs in the loop, placed off the contact frames; gaze matches travel; the face is not one drawing repeated.
items.item: The expression never changes and there is no blink anywhere in the loop — a frozen face passes lesser gates while reading dead.
items.name: expression-frozen-no-blink

items.inspect: Head-to-body ratio measured against the canon reference and reported; no non-uniform scaling anywhere in the figure. A fit achieved by squeezing fails.
items.item: Head (or any part) anisotropically squashed or stretched versus canon proportions — e.g. a face compressed to 82% width to make a crop fit.
items.name: head-proportions-distorted

items.inspect: Poses inspected on black AND on white before compositing. Any fringe is named with the poses it appears in, or the item fails.
items.item: White/light fringe or halo along cutout edges, left by keying, visible against dark grounds.
items.name: edge-fringe

items.inspect: Head, neck and collar read as one seated unit in every pose, including recoils. A visible perch wedge fails.
items.item: The head is perched: a bare wedge of neck shows between jaw and collar, like a ball on a post, instead of the neck seating into the collar.
items.name: head-perched-neck-wedge

items.inspect: Recoil poses (1 and 5 in an 8-pose cycle): the support knee folds FORWARD under load, the lifted leg's knee leads and the shin unfolds cleanly, and body height is at its lowest — verified visually, not only by the bob numbers.
items.item: At the recoil poses the support knee bows backward under the body's weight, the lifted leg tangles, and the body never actually drops to its low point.
items.name: recoil-knee-bows-backward

items.inspect: Across the cycle: a small charted lean into travel and counter-rotation against the hips (degrees stated), with the head steadier than the torso. A block that only slides fails.
items.item: The torso is a rigid sliding block: no lean into the travel, no counter-rotation against the hips — it translates sideways as one piece.
items.name: rigid-torso-block

items.inspect: Grade the finished artifact itself, at full size, against the canon reference — and grade only what is on screen. How a piece was made is never likeness evidence: which tool produced it, and whether the reference was regenerated on the way in, say nothing about whether the character on screen is true. A tool redrawing a character is not a demerit — an accurate redraw proves the tool is good at redrawing, and a redrawn version is often easier to rig, pose and animate than the raw file; judge a redraw on how true it is, never on the fact that it happened. Light thrown by a move or effect changing a character's colours is intended lighting — the show's lighting aim — not drift. (Owner ruling, 2026-10-28, from the Dreamina Water Orb correction; root cause of that bad grade: the owner's 'use our image and our likeness' was read as a literal file rule instead of its intent — the result must BE the character, true to likeness.)
items.item: The grade was decided from the production route instead of the picture: a rendition marked down because of which tool made it, or because its reference was regenerated on the way in, without the visible character being judged against the canon reference on its own — including effect light on the character misread as a defect (glowing fingertips read as claws; a move's light changing the character's colours read as drift).
items.name: graded-the-route-not-the-character

origin: The v7 walk-proof audit of record (2026-10-28). v7 was built from Mochiko's canon front art rearranged into a side walk; the owner's eye found more wrong with it than the delivery's list named, and the full audit of all 8 poses at full size produced these 20 items. Item 0 comes from the Wan frame-1 finding the same day: a generated run whose first frame was already a different character, misreported as drift.
title: Character audit checklist — the 20 points, plus item 0 for generated work
usage: Every character-work delivery is audited against EVERY item. Each item is marked pass / fail / na from inspection of the actual artifact (every member of a set, at full size — see show/production/WORKING-RULES.md rule 5). A fail is deliverable only when the self-judgment in the claims file names it (by this item's name or by 'item N') before any measurement is mentioned. delivery_gate.py enforces the marking and the naming; it does not do the looking.
